featured_videos.title: Give Me 8 Minutes. I'll Save You 10+ Years Of Carnivore Mistakes.
featured_videos.creator: Bart Kay - Health Science
featured_videos.editorial_title: Give Me 8 Minutes. I'll Save You 10+ Years Of Carnivore Mistakes.
featured_videos.commentary: Bart's hitting on something real here, and the comments are saying it loud: people are exhausted by the constant pivot-and-retry cycle. You see it everywhere in the community right now. Someone goes all-in on carnivore, hits a wall, then watches every influencer change their protocol weekly and feels like they're chasing a moving target. The thing is, most mistakes aren't about tweaking macros or adding an extra organ meat, they're about consistency and patience, which nobody wants to hear because it's not trendy. What's actually resonating in these comments is that Bart stayed steady, showed up, and didn't gaslight people into thinking they need the latest supplement stack or dietary hack to win. That's the real edge.

featured_videos.title: You'll Never Eat Sardines Again
featured_videos.creator: Paul Saladino MD
featured_videos.commentary: Paul's raising some legitimate concerns about canned sardines, but the community's got a point too. Heavy metals in small fish are genuinely less of an issue than in large predators, and modern canning standards (especially BPA-free options like Wild Planet) have actually improved. The real takeaway isn't "never eat sardines" but "pick your source carefully." Water or brine packed, minimal processing, and yes, grass-fed if you can find it. For most people eating sardines a few times a week, they're still one of the most nutrient-dense, affordable foods on the planet. Fear mongering doesn't help anyone make better decisions.

featured_videos.title: Why Everyone’s Leaving Carnivore
featured_videos.creator: Shawn Baker MD
featured_videos.commentary: The people actually staying on carnivore aren't the ones making headlines. They're the ones in the comments saying "six years, no plans to change" and "it's carnivore or nothing" because they got their health back. The real story isn't why people quit, it's why the ones who stick with it sound so certain. They're not debating science or trends, they're just living without the pain they used to have, and that's a hell of a lot quieter than the noise around quitting.

featured_videos.title: It Took Me 3 Years on Carnivore to Realize What I'll Tell You in 10 Minutes
featured_videos.creator: HomeSteadHow
featured_videos.editorial_title: It Took Me 3 Years on Carnivore to Realize What I'll Tell You in 10 Minutes
featured_videos.commentary:
There's a thread running through these comments that keeps hitting me. People aren't just losing weight or fixing their blood sugar, they're describing something deeper, a kind of reclamation. The 61-year-old swimmer who went from arrhythmia to endless energy in a month. The veteran who finally found something that doesn't trigger his autoimmune system. The guy who could unload two trucks solo and wasn't even hungry. This is what happens when you stop fighting your own biology.

But here's the friction point the comments expose, and it's real. The doctor's family dismisses it because "everyone would be using this." The cancer patient's worried about heart health from fatty red meat because that's what she learned. The propaganda runs deep, and it's anchored by credentials and authority, not evidence. Kerry's three-year journey to these insights probably includes watching people choose the comfortable lie over the uncomfortable truth, and that's the part nobody can shortcut for you. You have to be willing to question what you've been told.

featured_videos.title: You Can Eat Bread And Still Be Healthy (Carnivore Bread)
featured_videos.creator: Coach Carnivore Cam
featured_videos.editorial_title: You Can Eat Bread And Still Be Healthy (Carnivore Bread)
featured_videos.commentary: This recipe is blowing up in the comments for good reason, but notice what people are actually saying: some crushed it, others found it knocked them out of ketosis. That's the real story here. Egg white powder and cottage cheese have carbs, and if you're deep in carnivore for metabolic reasons, this is a "sometimes food" at best, not a daily staple. The people celebrating the crispy crust and the camping-trip convenience are being honest about what this is, and that's worth respecting. If you're missing bread texture or you're building a reintroduction strategy, the recipe works. But if you're doing carnivore because carbs derail you, this isn't your answer.

featured_videos.title: The "Biological Cost" of Ozempic & Mounjaro
featured_videos.creator: Kent Carnivore
featured_videos.commentary: The before-and-afters in this video are doing what Kent intended, they're making people uncomfortable, and that's because something's actually wrong. The comments nailing "body dysmorphia" and "they look sick, not healthy" are onto it, these drugs are creating a visual and metabolic cost that nobody's talking about at the yacht clubs where they're prescribed. You can't trick your brain into satiety for years without consequences, your bones thin out, your face hollows, and somewhere in that biological betrayal your body starts eating itself. The math the comment about lawsuits versus billions drives home what matters most: these companies already know the cost and decided it was worth paying in settlements.
